stories.headline: Twelve people, six of them minors, are hurt in a shooting outside Florida A&M’s stadium after its homecoming game
stories.summary: Twelve people were injured, 11 of them by gunfire, when shots rang out about 8 p.m. Saturday at an intersection next to Florida A&M University’s Bragg Memorial Stadium in Tallahassee, where the historically Black university had just hosted Arkansas-Pine Bluff for its homecoming game. Three victims were seriously hurt, including one minor; six of the injured are under 18 and the youngest is 11. Police Chief Lawrence Revell called it “an isolated incident between two or three individuals” that began as an altercation, said police believe one shooter was involved, and said no one had been arrested as of early Sunday. He praised officers who carried victims in their arms because vehicles could not get through the crowd, and asked witnesses to come forward. FAMU said the shooting happened on Perry Street near campus and that the campus was safe; nearby Florida State told people to stay indoors.

stories.headline: An Ohio village’s new mosque took hundreds of thousands from Uzbek-owned trucking firms with long safety-violation records, Fox finds
stories.summary: In part two of its series on trucking fraud in southwest Ohio, Fox News Digital reports that the Islamic Center of Maineville, under construction for four years in a Warren County village of about 1,400 people, has received substantial donations from Uzbek-owned trucking companies cited for serious safety and compliance violations. The mosque’s Telegram channel, which has about 3,600 members, posted screenshots of the gifts and showed ties to people identified as current or former Uzbek officials. One Springboro carrier gave at least $28,000 across 28 donations despite English-proficiency, invalid-CDL, logging-device and hours-of-service violations; another, with more than 100 violations including unsafe driving and invalid CDLs, gave at least $25,000. Republican state Rep. Michelle Teska is pushing legislation to crack down on truck drivers who cannot speak English. Part one traced the issue to a fatal crash by an Uzbek driver.

stories.headline: Terrible Towels at the Eiffel Tower: Steelers fans turn Paris black and gold before today’s first NFL game in France
stories.summary: A huge crowd of Pittsburgh Steelers fans gathered in front of the Eiffel Tower on Saturday, waving Terrible Towels on the eve of Sunday’s historic game against the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France, the NFL’s first regular-season game in Paris. Viewer videos sent to WTAE showed the black-and-gold crowd from the tower’s base and from a nearby bridge. Kickoff is 9:30 a.m. ET; WTAE is airing the game in Pittsburgh with a pregame special starting at 7 a.m. The fan gathering came a day after the league closed its “NFL House” fan venue in the city as protests swept France.

stories.headline: Connecticut towns are banning data centers before anyone has even proposed one
stories.summary: About half a dozen Connecticut municipalities have moved to block data center development with temporary moratoriums or outright bans, according to a CT Mirror review of meetings and records, even though almost no projects have been proposed. East Lyme’s Zoning Commission unanimously adopted an indefinite ban that took effect Saturday; New Haven passed a one-year moratorium in September with an exemption for its quantum computing hub; and tiny Morris has a two-year ban. Experts say Connecticut has never been attractive for big “hyperscale” sites because of high electricity costs and the need for large plots and utility access. A 2021 sales-tax break for projects investing at least $200 million has been used only once, for Cigna’s $386 million renovation of an existing data center in Windsor, and the state has reviewed just two applications. A planned facility next to the Millstone nuclear plant in Waterford died after local pushback. Trumbull has its own hearing on a proposed one-year moratorium.

stories.headline: Soldiers guard central Milan as youth protests spread across Europe, from Rome and Turin to Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana
stories.summary: Thousands of young people marched Saturday in Milan, Rome, Turin and other Italian cities as authorities flooded the streets with police and soldiers to head off a repeat of last weekend’s looting. Milan stayed peaceful, but there were brief clashes with police in Rome and Turin. Premier Giorgia Meloni sent another 500 soldiers to Milan on top of hundreds already there, backing about 5,000 police, and announced tougher penalties for minors, who police say made up much of last week’s violent crowds; several minors were detained in Milan as a precaution. Luxury boutiques including Gucci, Tiffany and Omega boarded up, and the Apple store stayed closed. Right-wing student groups also marched in Rome against the left-wing protests. Large demonstrations hit Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana as well, over issues ranging from education and corruption to anti-war causes, pensions and housing.

stories.headline: Apple says it wants to fix Safari’s cramped layout on the iPhone Duo’s outer screen — and adds book-style two-page PDFs
stories.summary: Apple is looking at ways to let websites use more of the iPhone Duo’s short, wide outer display, where Safari’s controls sit along the side and pages are currently squeezed into the area beside them. In a WebKit post on Friday, Apple’s Jen Simmons said the existing viewport-fit=cover setting could let pages extend under the controls, but Apple’s research found many sites don’t leave enough room around key content, so parts of the page would be hidden. Apple is exploring an alternative, such as letting a header’s background span the screen while its links stay clear of the controls. For now Safari 27.1 fills the leftover strip with the page’s background color. Safari 27.1 also shows PDFs as two pages when the Duo is held half-folded like a book, and developers can test experimental fold-posture detection behind feature flags.

stories.headline: Ricky Warwick on passing out in a pool of glass and blood at Lemmy’s party — “Warwick, you’re a lightweight, you’ll never make it”
stories.summary: The Almighty, Thin Lizzy and Black Star Riders singer Ricky Warwick, who turned 60 this summer on the day he played Iron Maiden’s Eddfest at Knebworth, shares stories from 46 years in rock as he releases his new solo album, Fire & Vengeance. The best involves Lemmy: in 1991, ahead of The Almighty’s tour with Motörhead, Warwick arrived jet-lagged at an LA hotel to find a party in Lemmy’s room, where Lemmy handed him a pint of Jack and Coke and played him the just-mixed 1916 album. As it ended Warwick stood up, collapsed face-first, cut his eyebrow on the shattered glass and threw up, only to hear Lemmy say he was a lightweight who would never make it. He also tells of David Bowie walking into his dressing room, being smacked on the head by Alice Cooper, a quiet drink with Steve Harris, and run-ins with Metallica and Guns N’ Roses.

stories.headline: Charlotte police pull over two men riding a full-size couch down the street on a pair of Lime e-scooters
stories.summary: Charlotte-Mecklenburg police stopped two men cruising down South Tryon Street on what appeared to be a full-size sofa perched across two Lime shared electric scooters. “Well, this was certainly a first,” the department posted. “Yes, an actual couch.” It isn’t clear how the scooters were attached or how the pair steered, but they got far enough to catch officers’ attention. Police said they appreciated the creativity but reminded people to think about safety “no matter what you’re ‘driving’ (using that term extremely loosely),” adding that it was “probably best to leave the mobile furniture displays to IKEA.” Police did not say whether either man was cited or name them.

stories.headline: Koivunen wins it in overtime after Rakell ties it with 1:06 left as the Penguins rally past the Predators 3-2
stories.summary: Ville Koivunen scored 3:44 into overtime and the Pittsburgh Penguins came back to beat the Nashville Predators 3-2 at PPG Paints Arena on Saturday night, their second straight win after a four-game losing streak. Koivunen briefly lost the puck before collecting it and skating into the high slot for a snap shot. Rickard Rakell forced overtime at 18:54 of the third period, one-timing a cross-ice pass from Sidney Crosby for his second goal in three games after a nine-game drought to open the season. Connor Dewar also scored, 18 seconds into the second period, and Arturs Silovs made 24 saves. Steven Stamkos and Jayden Struble scored for Nashville, and Juuse Saros stopped 34 shots. Evgeni Malkin, tied with Nick Robertson for the team lead with six goals, sat out with an illness. The Penguins are now 5-6-1 and have earned points in nine straight meetings with the Predators (8-0-2).

stories.headline: A massive Ukrainian drone swarm hits Belgorod overnight, reportedly targeting the city’s biggest shopping mall, a day after Starlink speeds were restored
stories.summary: A large swarm of Ukrainian drones attacked the Russian border city of Belgorod overnight into Oct. 25, according to local officials and eyewitness video. Locals said most of the drones converged on the city center, and the monitoring channel Exilenova-Plus said the target was MegaGRINN, Belgorod’s largest shopping and entertainment complex, with more than 200 stores, a supermarket and a cinema. The center was closed and empty at the time. Regional authorities confirmed a “massive UAV attack,” said one civilian was killed and 10 were injured, and told residents to stay indoors as attacks continued; residents also reported a fire in the courtyard of a nearby apartment complex. The Kyiv Independent said it could not independently verify the reports. Belgorod sits about 21 miles from the Ukrainian border and is a frequent target. The strike came a day after Ukraine said its Starshield satellite service, throttled since Oct. 14, had been restored to full speed, helping troops coordinate drone attacks.

stories.headline: The Archdiocese of New York agrees to pay $800 million to about 1,300 people who say they were sexually abused by clergy and lay workers
stories.summary: The Archdiocese of New York has agreed to pay $800 million to settle claims from some 1,300 people who say they were sexually abused by clergy members and lay workers, one of the largest settlements of its kind in the Catholic Church. Jeff Anderson, whose firm represents more than 250 of the plaintiffs, said the deal is final pending signed paperwork and that all plaintiffs have agreed to it. In an email to priests on Saturday, Archbishop Ronald Hicks said an agreement had been reached and that the archdiocese was “on the verge of being able to, please God, bring some measure of healing and reconciliation to all victim-survivors,” and to turn its attention back to its mission. Anderson said his clients feel both sorrow and “a real sense of relief and achievement.” The archdiocese entered mediation in December 2025 and had laid off staff and planned to sell Manhattan properties to raise $300 million. In 2024 the Archdiocese of Los Angeles agreed to an $880 million settlement.

stories.headline: An Alabama man said he found his wife dead of a self-inflicted gunshot in his Tesla — grainy security video helped convict him of capital murder
stories.summary: On Nov. 15, 2022, David Tolbert told Huntsville, Alabama, police he had opened the door of his red Tesla outside the store where he worked and found his wife, 37-year-old Savannah Tolbert, dead in the passenger seat with a gun in her right hand. Investigators quickly doubted it was a suicide: the gun was in her right hand but the wound was on the left side of the back of her head, a shell casing was found on the rear seat, and the retired corrections officer tested positive for gunshot residue. The couple had been living apart, and police learned he was having an affair with a woman he had coached on her own Tesla. Detectives synced the store’s cameras with distant, grainy parking-lot video from a neighboring pool store, which showed Savannah getting into the car and, about 20 minutes later, a figure investigators identified as David at the driver’s door before the taillights flashed. His explanation for the residue, a toy cannon in the trunk, didn’t match the video. A jury convicted him, and he is serving life without parole, “48 Hours” reports.

stories.headline: Tesla’s new Roadster makes its first public appearance at LA’s Petersen Museum — look, don’t touch, through Tuesday
stories.summary: Tesla’s new Roadster is on display at the Petersen Automotive Museum in Los Angeles from Oct. 24 through Oct. 27 in the main lobby, the public’s first chance to see the car since its unveiling at SpaceX’s McGregor, Texas, test site earlier this month. The museum lists it as the 2028 Tesla Roadster Thrust Prototype — not the invite-only Rocket version that drove upside down at the reveal — and calls it Tesla’s “last best driver’s car.” Tesla plans four trims: the standard car makes about 1,340 horsepower; Performance adds suction fans and adaptive suspension for 0-60 mph in under 1.6 seconds; Thrust adds a cold-gas thruster system with four rear nozzles that hit 0-60 in 0.81 seconds at the unveiling; and the single-seat Rocket adds more nozzles and can briefly fly. Thrust is the trim original Founders Series reservations were converted to. The exhibit is roped off, so visitors can only look and take photos, and the prototype has no side mirrors, though U.S. production cars will. Production is set for 2028, with refundable deposits of $50,000 for Performance and $250,000 for Thrust.

stories.headline: Marty Friedman: Nick Menza’s drumming is “a huge reason why we weren’t just kind of an underground thrash metal band”
stories.summary: Former Megadeth guitarist Marty Friedman told Chile’s La Pajarera podcast that the late drummer Nick Menza deserves more credit for the band’s mainstream success. “A big reason why Megadeth became as popular in the mainstream as we did was because of Nick,” Friedman said. “Nick’s playing is not a typical thrash metal drummer style. It’s very mainstream… there’s not a lot of heavy metal clichés.” Combined with Dave Mustaine’s riffs, he said, Menza’s beat “elevated us to stadium level.” Menza collapsed behind his kit from a heart attack during a 2016 show with the band OHM at the Baked Potato in Studio City, California, and was pronounced dead at the hospital. Mustaine has said he wanted Menza and Friedman back in Megadeth after Chris Broderick and Shawn Drover left in 2014; Menza began working on new material but walked away over what he called a “very unfair” contract, about a year and a half before he died.

stories.headline: Trump and the first lady vote early in person in Palm Beach on Florida’s first day of early voting, then head to a Georgia rally
stories.summary: President Trump and first lady Melania Trump cast their midterm ballots in person Saturday at the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections building, on the first day of Florida’s early voting, which runs through Halloween. Earlier in the week the president had said he prefers to vote on Election Day, and in recent elections he has voted by mail even while criticizing widespread mail-in voting. After voting he flew to Perry, Georgia, for a rally backing Republican Reps. Mike Collins and Rick Jackson, calling them “two incredible people” and writing on Truth Social that their opponents “want to Take Away Your Guns, Open Your Borders, Allow Men To Play In Women’s Sports.” Trump has been on the road most days this week, with stops in South Carolina on Wednesday, Iowa on Thursday and Fort Myers, Florida, on Friday; his Election Day plans have not been announced.

stories.headline: Musk now admits SpaceX throttled Ukraine’s Starlink, saying Kyiv broke the terms by using it for offensive drone strikes
stories.summary: Elon Musk said Saturday that SpaceX throttled Starlink service in Ukraine, after days of questions over who ordered the slowdown that disrupted front-line drone operations for more than a week. “Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be,” Musk wrote on X. “Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week.” He maintained that the U.S. government controls changes to Starshield, SpaceX’s military-grade version that has become the backbone of Ukraine’s drone and communications network, and defended SpaceX’s role since 2022. President Trump had said he did not make the call. Musk’s post came after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said speeds were restored overnight to pre-restriction levels, helping logistics and defense against Russia’s jet-powered Shahed drones. The restoration comes as Russia agreed to resume three-way talks with Washington and Kyiv next month, and a day after a localized ceasefire around Oleshky brokered by first lady Melania Trump.

stories.headline: France-style rioting spreads to Barcelona as hooded youths torch bins and try to loot a Foot Locker: “People were bored at home”
stories.summary: Hundreds of mostly young, hooded rioters dressed in black descended on central Barcelona on Saturday afternoon, smashing bus shelters, setting trash cans on fire, firing fireworks and flares at police and building barricades out of city bicycles, La Vanguardia reported. The gathering, billed vaguely as a protest “against the system,” was organized on social media without city approval, and some businesses closed early and locked their doors, at times trapping shoppers inside. “People were bored at home and came here, like in France,” one youth was quoted as saying; another said, “We’re not protesting about anything.” A third shouted, “Let’s all go to Foot Locker!”, though the store had already shut. A Vanguardia reporter described a crowd speaking Arabic, French, Spanish and Catalan that “basically sought to get free sneakers.” Catalonia’s leader, Salvador Illa, said the violence “has no place” in the city and vowed those responsible will pay; Catalan police confirmed arrests without giving a number. The unrest came as nationwide protests in France on Saturday led to more than 1,000 arrests, after copycat violence in Brussels and Milan in recent weeks.

stories.headline: Courts extend Second Amendment protection to switchblades and body armor as the Supreme Court readies its AR-15 ban case
stories.summary: Two federal rulings on Wednesday extended Second Amendment protection beyond firearms, energizing gun-rights advocates ahead of a Supreme Court showdown over bans on AR-15-style rifles. The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals held that a federal law restricting interstate commerce in switchblade knives violates the Second Amendment, and a federal judge in the Western District of New York struck down the state’s restrictions on personal body armor; both courts found the items qualify as constitutionally protected “arms.” The Supreme Court is preparing to hear Viramontes v. Cook County, which could decide whether AR-15-style rifles are protected. Dudley Brown, president of the National Association for Gun Rights, which filed an amicus brief, told Fox News Digital that both lower-court cases will “really be decided” by the Viramontes ruling, and that a decision against AR-15 bans could shape challenges to limits on magazines, automatic knives and body armor. The rulings rest on the Heller and Bruen decisions, which protect weapons in common lawful use while allowing restrictions on “dangerous and unusual” arms.

stories.headline: Trumbull’s Kids Pumpkin Fest is Sunday on the Town Hall Green with pumpkin decorating, a live DJ and touch-a-truck
stories.summary: Trumbull’s annual Kids Pumpkin Fest runs this Sunday, Oct. 25, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. on the Town Hall Green at 5866 Main Street, Patch reports. The free family event features pumpkin decorating, face painting, lawn games, crafts and a live DJ, plus a touch-a-truck with the Long Hill Fire and Trumbull Police departments and crafts with the Trumbull Nature and Arts Center. Mobile coffee trailer Brewberry Cafe will serve a seasonal menu.

stories.headline: Trumbull this week: a hearing on a one-year data center moratorium, early voting opens Monday at the library, and a Town Hall Halloween parade
stories.summary: Trumbull’s Planning and Zoning Commission will hold a public hearing Wednesday on a proposed text amendment that would define data centers as their own principal use in the town’s zoning rules and put a one-year moratorium on them, according to the meeting agenda, Patch reports in its weekly look at what’s coming up in town. Early voting for the Nov. 3 election runs Monday, Oct. 19, through Sunday, Nov. 1, at the Trumbull Library, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., with longer 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. hours on Oct. 27 and Oct. 29, according to the town clerk. Patch also points to First Selectman Vicki Tesoro’s statement on the proposed high-density housing development at 1, 7 and 15 Main St. in Monroe, near the Coventry Lane area of Trumbull; no application is pending in Trumbull, and residents can send comments to the Monroe Planning and Zoning Commission. The Commission on Aging will hear an update on fraud prevention and a Senior Center report, and preschoolers can trick-or-treat through Town Hall in the annual Halloween parade, which has two sessions of 20 children each and requires registration.
